questions.prompt: What is the traditional Sinhala and Tamil New Year festival called?
questions.explanation: Aluth Avurudda, the Sinhala and Tamil New Year, is celebrated in mid-April and is Sri Lanka's most widely observed cultural festival.

questions.prompt: Which Sri Lankan city hosts the annual Esala Perahera procession?
questions.explanation: The Esala Perahera is held in Kandy and honours the Sacred Tooth Relic housed at the Temple of the Tooth.

questions.prompt: Pol sambol, a staple Sri Lankan side dish, is made mainly from which ingredient?
questions.explanation: 'Pol' means coconut in Sinhala. Pol sambol combines scraped coconut with chilli, lime, onion and Maldive fish.

questions.prompt: Which festival commemorates the birth, enlightenment and passing of the Buddha?
questions.explanation: Vesak falls on the full moon of May and is marked across Sri Lanka with lanterns and free food stalls called dansal.

questions.prompt: What is the national flower of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The blue water lily, known locally as Nil Manel, was designated Sri Lanka's national flower in 1986.

questions.prompt: Which was the first ancient capital of Sri Lanka and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: Anuradhapura served as the island's capital for over a thousand years from around the 4th century BCE.

questions.prompt: Which drum is central to traditional Kandyan dance?
questions.explanation: The Geta Bera is a double-headed drum played at the waist and is the signature instrument of up-country Kandyan dance.

questions.prompt: Sri Lanka is the world's leading producer of which spice?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka produces the great majority of the world's true cinnamon, long traded internationally as Ceylon cinnamon.

questions.prompt: Sigiriya, the rock fortress, was built during the reign of which king?
questions.explanation: Kashyapa I made Sigiriya his royal citadel in the 5th century CE after seizing the throne from his father.

questions.prompt: The vast Parakrama Samudra reservoir is credited to which Sri Lankan king?
questions.explanation: Parakramabahu I built the reservoir at Polonnaruwa in the 12th century, reflecting his principle that no rainwater should reach the sea unused.

questions.prompt: How many players from one team are on the field during a cricket match?
questions.explanation: A cricket side fields eleven players, with substitutes permitted only for fielding in most formats.

questions.prompt: How many legal deliveries make up a standard cricket over?
questions.explanation: A standard over consists of six legal deliveries; wides and no-balls must be bowled again.

questions.prompt: What is it called when a bowler takes three wickets in three consecutive deliveries?
questions.explanation: The term hat-trick originated in 19th-century cricket, when a bowler achieving the feat was rewarded with a hat.

questions.prompt: Which country won the 1996 Cricket World Cup?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka beat Australia in the 1996 final in Lahore, winning their first World Cup title.

questions.prompt: Who captained Sri Lanka to victory in the 1996 Cricket World Cup?
questions.explanation: Arjuna Ranatunga led the side, while Aravinda de Silva scored an unbeaten century in the final.

questions.prompt: Which Test cricket series is contested between England and Australia?
questions.explanation: The Ashes dates from 1882, when a mock obituary declared English cricket dead and its ashes taken to Australia.

questions.prompt: Who was the first male cricketer to score a double century in a One Day International?
questions.explanation: Tendulkar made 200 not out against South Africa at Gwalior in February 2010.

questions.prompt: Which bowler holds the record for the most wickets in Test cricket?
questions.explanation: Muralitharan finished his Test career with 800 wickets, the highest total in the format's history.

questions.prompt: What is the national sport of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: Volleyball was declared Sri Lanka's national sport in 1991, although cricket draws far larger audiences.

questions.prompt: Which batter holds the highest individual Test score made by a Sri Lankan?
questions.explanation: Jayawardene scored 374 against South Africa in Colombo in 2006.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants absorb from the air during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: Babies are born with around 270 bones, many of which fuse during growth to leave 206 in adulthood.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: An adult's skin covers roughly two square metres and accounts for about 15 percent of body weight.

questions.prompt: Which animal is the fastest over land?
questions.explanation: A cheetah can reach around 100 kilometres per hour, though only in short bursts.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
questions.explanation: The symbol K comes from kalium, the Latin name for the element.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell contains most of its DNA?
questions.explanation: The nucleus houses chromosomal DNA, although mitochondria carry a small separate genome.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the shortest day in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Despite being the largest planet, Jupiter rotates once in just under ten hours.

questions.prompt: Approximately how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: The exact figure is 299,792,458 metres per second, a fixed constant used to define the metre.

questions.prompt: Which element is the most abundant in the Earth's crust by mass?
questions.explanation: Oxygen makes up roughly 46 percent of the crust by mass, bound up in silicate minerals.

questions.prompt: Which metal has the highest melting point?
questions.explanation: Tungsten melts at about 3,422 degrees Celsius, which is why it was used for incandescent lamp filaments.

questions.prompt: The line “May the Force be with you” comes from which film series?
questions.explanation: The phrase recurs throughout the Star Wars saga, first appearing in the 1977 original film.

questions.prompt: Which singer is widely known as the “King of Pop”?
questions.explanation: The title became closely associated with Jackson during the success of his album Thriller.

questions.prompt: In The Lion King, what is the name of the young lion who is heir to the throne?
questions.explanation: Simba means lion in Swahili, the language behind several names in the film.

questions.prompt: Frodo Baggins is a central character in which film trilogy?
questions.explanation: Frodo is played by Elijah Wood in Peter Jackson's adaptation of Tolkien's novels.

questions.prompt: Which studio produced the animated film Spirited Away?
questions.explanation: Spirited Away was directed by Hayao Miyazaki and won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

questions.prompt: Who directed the 1993 film Jurassic Park?
questions.explanation: Spielberg combined animatronics with early computer-generated imagery to create the dinosaurs.

questions.prompt: Which band released the album Abbey Road?
questions.explanation: Abbey Road was released in 1969 and was the last album the band recorded together.

questions.prompt: Which actor played Tony Stark in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
questions.explanation: Downey Jr. first appeared as Tony Stark in Iron Man in 2008.

questions.prompt: Which film won the Academy Award for Best Picture at the 2020 ceremony?
questions.explanation: Parasite was the first film not in the English language to win Best Picture.

questions.prompt: Who composed the musical score for the film Inception?
questions.explanation: Zimmer built the score around a slowed-down sample of the Edith Piaf song used in the film.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Japan?
questions.explanation: Tokyo became the capital in 1868, replacing Kyoto.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of the Earth's surface, more than all land combined.

questions.prompt: How many continents are there on Earth?
questions.explanation: The seven are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, Oceania and South America.

questions.prompt: In which country would you find the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal stands at Agra and was completed in the mid-17th century as a mausoleum.

questions.prompt: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The yen was adopted in 1871 as part of Japan's modernisation of its monetary system.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the city of Cairo?
questions.explanation: Cairo grew along the Nile near the point where the river fans out into its delta.

questions.prompt: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest mountain at about 5,895 metres.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City covers roughly 0.49 square kilometres within the city of Rome.

questions.prompt: Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake, lies in which country?
questions.explanation: Baikal reaches over 1,600 metres deep and holds around a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
questions.explanation: The Bering Strait is about 82 kilometres wide at its narrowest point, between Russia and Alaska.
